subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equations of the tangents to the hyperbola x² − 4y² = 4 which (i) are parallel to x + 2y = 0, (ii) are perpendicular to x + 2y = 0.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.66 — SAQ chapter 9 Hyperbola, answer 79.1, the first of a printed twin pair (79.1/79.2). On a ★★ SSP page (p.66 is listed on p.49's 13-page SSP list; chapter banner and table both read ★★). Printed appearances: AP 19 · TS 15. Two-column page, no printed mark tags — the 2+2 split (parallel/perpendicular) here is OURS, matching the natural two-part shape of the question. FINDING: the book's printed working for part (i) — 'y = −x/2 ± √(4(1/4) − 1) ⇒ y = −x/2 ⇒ x + 2y = 0' (book p.66) — is presented as an ordinary tangent, but it is mathematically degenerate: the given line x + 2y = 0 is one of the two asymptotes of x² − 4y² = 4 (asymptote slopes are ±b/a = ±1/2, and the given line's slope is exactly −1/2), and no finite point on a hyperbola ever has a tangent slope equal to its asymptote slope (the tangent slope b²x/(a²y) approaches ±b/a only in the limit as the point recedes to infinity — a hyperbola gets arbitrarily close to its asymptote but never touches it). This card keeps the book's mechanically-derived boxed result for part (i) — since that is what the mark scheme rewards — but the step's `why` and this note record that it is not a genuine tangent. Part (ii) has no such issue: slope 2 is not an asymptote slope, so y = 2x ± √15 are two genuine tangent lines, matching the book. Hyperbola is a SAQ+VSAQ-only unit on the book's IPE Blue Print (book p.5) — 4 marks in Section B (paper slot Q15) and 2 marks in Section A (paper slot Q5); it has NO LAQ chapter and no Section-C slot, so no 7-mark form is authored for this unit. insider_note: This question is built around a special case: the given line x + 2y = 0 is exactly one of the hyperbola's own asymptotes, so a tangent 'parallel' to it does not really exist — write the examiner-marked mechanical result down for the marks, but be ready to explain in words that it is the asymptote itself, not a true tangent.

steps.label: Set up the tangent formula
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own — every result below substitutes into this formula.
steps.memory_tip: Start every hyperbola tangent-parallel/perpendicular question the same way: standard form, tangent-with-slope-m formula, then the given line's own slope.
lines: Divide by 4: x²/4 − y²/1 = 1 ⇒ a² = 4, b² = 1
Tangent with slope m: y = mx ± √(a²m² − b²)
Slope of the given line x + 2y = 0: m = −1/2
steps.why: Every 'tangent parallel/perpendicular to a line' question starts the same way: write the hyperbola's tangent-with-slope-m formula, then read the given line's own slope off it.
common_mistakes: Using the ellipse tangent formula y = mx ± √(a²m² + b²) — a hyperbola SUBTRACTS b², it does not add it.
Reading the slope of x + 2y = 0 as +1/2 instead of −1/2.

steps.label: Parallel tangent
steps.margin_note: Two marks. This case is degenerate — see the why for this step.
steps.memory_tip: If the root under the tangent formula collapses to zero, check whether the given slope IS an asymptote slope ±b/a.
lines: Parallel tangent has the same slope m = −1/2
steps.why: Substituting m = −1/2 into the tangent formula makes the term under the root vanish (4m² − b² = 0) — that happens exactly because −1/2 is the SLOPE OF AN ASYMPTOTE of this hyperbola (asymptote slopes are ±b/a = ±1/2), and no genuine tangent line is ever parallel to an asymptote.
common_mistakes: Treating the line x + 2y = 0 that comes out of the formula as a real tangent point — it is the asymptote itself, which the hyperbola gets arbitrarily close to but never touches.
Not noticing that a zero under the root here is a special case (the given line's slope equals an asymptote slope), not a coincidence to ignore.

steps.label: Perpendicular tangent
steps.margin_note: Two marks. This case is a genuine, ordinary tangent pair.
steps.memory_tip: The negative reciprocal of −1/2 is 2, not −2.
lines: Slope of the perpendicular is the negative
steps.why: Slope 2 is not an asymptote slope (the asymptotes have slope ±1/2), so the tangent formula gives two genuine tangent lines here.
common_mistakes: Taking the negative reciprocal of −1/2 incorrectly (it is 2, not −2).
Dropping the ± sign and reporting only one of the two tangent lines.
